items.stem: What is the exact value of sin 7π/6?
items.markingKey: D. 7π/6 lies in quadrant 3; using the reference angle and the sign of sin there gives −1/2.

items.stem: Explain why −1 ≤ sin θ ≤ 1 for every real θ.
items.answer: sin θ is the y-coordinate of a point on the unit circle (radius 1), so it can never be further than 1 from 0 on the vertical axis.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: sin θ is the y-coordinate of a point on the unit circle (radius 1), so it can never be further than 1 from 0 on the vertical axis. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: A student claims: "cos(−π/3) = −1/2 because the angle is negative." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: A negative angle is measured clockwise; −π/3 is in quadrant 4 where cosine is positive, so cos(−π/3) = 1/2 (cosine is even).
items.markingKey: A negative angle is measured clockwise; −π/3 is in quadrant 4 where cosine is positive, so cos(−π/3) = 1/2 (cosine is even). 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Find the exact value of tan(2π) + 4sin(3π/4).
items.markingKey: Each exact trigonometric value correct (A1 each, may be implied); combined and simplified: 2√2 (A1). No calculator: decimals score A0.

items.stem: Points A and B lie on the unit circle at angles 5π/6 and 7π/6 respectively (measured anticlockwise from the positive x-axis). Find the exact distance AB.
Points A and B lie on the unit circle at angles 7π/4 and π/4 respectively (measured anticlockwise from the positive x-axis). Find the exact distance AB.

The points A and B lie on the unit circle with centre O, where angle AOx = π/2 and angle BOx = 5π/6 (both measured anticlockwise from the positive x-axis).
(a) Write down the exact coordinates of A and B.
(b) Find the exact size of angle AOB.
(c) Find the exact area of triangle AOB.
(d) Show that AB² = 2 − 2cos(AOB) and hence find AB² exactly.
items.markingKey: (a) A1 A1. (b) 5π/6 − π/2 = π/3 A1. (c) ½(1)(1)sin(π/3) M1 = √3/4 A1. (d) cosine rule with OA = OB = 1: AB² = 1 + 1 − 2cos AOB M1 AG; = 1 A1.

items.stem:
The angle θ satisfies tan θ = −20/21 and π/2 < θ < π.
(a) Find the exact value of cos θ.
(b) Find the exact value of sin θ.
(c) Hence find the exact value of sin θ + cos θ and state, with a reason, its sign.
items.markingKey: Right-angled triangle with sides 20, 21, hypotenuse 29 (M1); sign of cos in quadrant 2 (R1) cos θ = −21/29 (A1); sin θ = 20/29 (A1); sum −1/29 (A1), sign follows (R1).

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The ratio sin θ / cos θ, i.e. the gradient of the radius to the point (cos θ, sin θ); undefined when cos θ = 0"?
items.markingKey: B. This is the definition of tan θ (unit circle definition).

items.stem: Which of the following is the exact value of sin(7π/4)?
items.markingKey: C. 7π/4 is in quadrant 4 with reference angle π/4, sine negative.

items.stem: Using the unit circle, explain why tan(11π/6) is negative and hence write down its exact value.
items.markingKey: 11π/6 lies in quadrant 4 (R1); the reference angle is π/6 (A1); in quadrant 4 the ratio y/x-value makes tan negative (R1); so tan(11π/6) = −√3/3 (A1).

items.stem: Without a calculator, explain why tan(3π/4) = −tan(π/4).
items.markingKey: 3π/4 lies in quadrant 2 (R1); the reference angle is π/4 (A1); in quadrant 2 the ratio y/x-value makes tan negative (R1); so tan(3π/4) = −1 (A1).

items.stem: Find the exact value of −2cos(π) − 2cos(2π/3).
items.markingKey: Each exact trigonometric value correct (A1 each, may be implied); combined and simplified: 3 (A1). No calculator: decimals score A0.

items.stem: "cos(−π/3) = −1/2 because the angle is negative." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: A negative angle is measured clockwise; −π/3 is in quadrant 4 where cosine is positive, so cos(−π/3) = 1/2 (cosine is even).
items.markingKey: A negative angle is measured clockwise; −π/3 is in quadrant 4 where cosine is positive, so cos(−π/3) = 1/2 (cosine is even). 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Points A and B lie on the unit circle at angles π/4 and 7π/4 respectively (measured anticlockwise from the positive x-axis). Find the exact distance AB.

The points A and B lie on the unit circle with centre O, where angle AOx = π/3 and angle BOx = π/2 (both measured anticlockwise from the positive x-axis).
(a) Write down the exact coordinates of A and B.
(b) Find the exact size of angle AOB.
(c) Find the exact area of triangle AOB.
(d) Show that AB² = 2 − 2cos(AOB) and hence find AB² exactly.
items.markingKey: (a) A1 A1. (b) π/2 − π/3 = π/6 A1. (c) ½(1)(1)sin(π/6) M1 = 1/4 A1. (d) cosine rule with OA = OB = 1: AB² = 1 + 1 − 2cos AOB M1 AG; = 2 − √3 A1.

items.stem:
The points A and B lie on the unit circle with centre O, where angle AOx = 5π/6 and angle BOx = 3π/2 (both measured anticlockwise from the positive x-axis).
(a) Write down the exact coordinates of A and B.
(b) Find the exact size of angle AOB.
(c) Find the exact area of triangle AOB.
(d) Show that AB² = 2 − 2cos(AOB) and hence find AB² exactly.
items.markingKey: (a) A1 A1. (b) 3π/2 − 5π/6 = 2π/3 A1. (c) ½(1)(1)sin(2π/3) M1 = √3/4 A1. (d) cosine rule with OA = OB = 1: AB² = 1 + 1 − 2cos AOB M1 AG; = 3 A1.

items.stem: Which expression is identical to 1 − cos²x?
items.markingKey: sin²x. From sin²x + cos²x = 1.

items.stem: Explain why knowing sin θ alone is not enough to find cos θ uniquely.
items.answer: cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ gives two square roots ±; the quadrant of θ is needed to choose the sign.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ gives two square roots ±; the quadrant of θ is needed to choose the sign. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: A student claims: "sin²x means sin(x²)." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: sin²x means (sin x)²; sin(x²) is the sine of x squared, a different function.
items.markingKey: sin²x means (sin x)²; sin(x²) is the sine of x squared, a different function. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: If cos α = 1/4, find the exact value of cos 2α, showing which identity you use.
items.markingKey: Choose cos 2θ = 2cos²θ − 1 (M1); substitute 1/4 (A1); −7/8 (A1). No need to find the quadrant: only cos² appears.

items.stem: Given that sin θ = 20/29 and π/2 < θ < π, find the exact value of (a) cos θ (b) tan θ.
items.markingKey: Use sin²θ + cos²θ = 1: cos²θ = 1 − (20/29)² = 441/841 (M1); choose the sign for quadrant 2 (R1); cos θ = −21/29 (A1); tan θ = sin θ/cos θ = −20/21 (A1).

items.stem: It is given that sin θ = 9/41, where π/2 < θ < π. Find the exact value of sin 2θ.
items.markingKey: Other ratio by Pythagoras with correct sign: sin θ = 9/41, cos θ = −40/41 (M1 A1); double angle identity used (M1); −720/1681 (A1).

items.stem:
Let sin θ = 3/5, where π/2 < θ < π.
(a) Find cos θ.
(b) Hence find the exact value of 4 sin θ cos θ + 1 cos 2θ.
items.markingKey: (a) cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ (M1), negative/positive by quadrant 2 (R1), −4/5 (A1). (b) sin θ cos θ = −12/25, cos 2θ = 7/25 (A1 A1); −41/25 (A1).

items.stem:
The acute angle θ is such that cos θ = 12/13.
(a) Find the exact value of sin θ.
(b) Find the exact values of sin 2θ and cos 2θ.
(c) Hence find the exact value of cos 4θ and of sin 4θ.
(d) Determine, with a reason, whether 4θ is acute or obtuse given that 0 < 4θ < π.
items.markingKey: (a) Pythagoras, acute so positive: 5/13 A1. (b) M1 A1 A1. (c) cos 4θ = 2cos²2θ − 1 M1 = −239/28561 A1; sin 4θ = 2 sin 2θ cos 2θ = 28560/28561 A1. (d) cos 4θ < 0 so 4θ is obtuse R1. Total 8 marks. [Valid only when 0 < 4θ < π; check with θ = arccos(12/13) ≈ 0.395.]

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "double angle identities for cosine"?
options: Cot x = cos x / sin x = 1/tan x, defined where sin x ≠ 0
An identity such as sin(π/2 − θ) = cos θ or cos(π/2 − θ) = sin θ relating complementary angles
A function with f(−x) = −f(x) for all x in its domain; its graph has rotational symmetry of order 2 about the origin (e.g. sin x, tan x)
items.markingKey: A. "double angle identities for cosine" is the identities cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ = 2cos²θ − 1 = 1 − 2sin²θ.

items.stem: Explain why cos 2θ has three equivalent forms.
items.answer: Start from cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ; replacing sin²θ by 1 − cos²θ gives 2cos²θ − 1, replacing cos²θ by 1 − sin²θ gives 1 − 2sin²θ.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Start from cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ; replacing sin²θ by 1 − cos²θ gives 2cos²θ − 1, replacing cos²θ by 1 − sin²θ gives 1 − 2sin²θ. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Lukas claims that sin 2x = sin²x for all x. Use x = π/4 to show that the claim is false, and state the correct identity.
items.answer: At x = π/4: left side 1, right side 1/2; not equal.
items.markingKey: Left side evaluated exactly = 1 (A1); right side = 1/2 (A1); since they differ the statement is not an identity (R1); correct identity stated (A1).

items.stem: Explain why sin²x = (1 − cos 2x)/2 and use it to write sin²(3x) in terms of cos 6x.
items.markingKey: cos 2x = 1 − 2sin²x rearranged (R1); replace x by 3x (M1); (1 − cos 6x)/2 (A1).

items.stem: It is given that sin θ = 9/41, where 0 < θ < π/2. Find the exact value of sin 2θ.
items.markingKey: Other ratio by Pythagoras with correct sign: sin θ = 9/41, cos θ = 40/41 (M1 A1); double angle identity used (M1); 720/1681 (A1).

items.stem: The acute angle β has cos β = 5/6. Calculate the exact value of cos 2β.
items.markingKey: Choose cos 2θ = 2cos²θ − 1 (M1); substitute 5/6 (A1); 7/18 (A1). No need to find the quadrant: only cos² appears.

items.stem: A student claims: "If sin θ = 3/5 then cos θ = 4/5." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: cos θ = ±4/5; it is −4/5 if θ is obtuse (quadrant 2), so the quadrant must be stated.
items.markingKey: cos θ = ±4/5; it is −4/5 if θ is obtuse (quadrant 2), so the quadrant must be stated. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
Let sin θ = −7/25, where π < θ < 3π/2.
(a) Find cos θ.
(b) Hence find the exact value of 4 sin θ cos θ + 4 cos 2θ.
items.markingKey: (a) cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ (M1), negative/positive by quadrant 3 (R1), −24/25 (A1). (b) sin θ cos θ = 168/625, cos 2θ = 527/625 (A1 A1); 556/125 (A1).

items.stem:
Let sin θ = −7/25, where 3π/2 < θ < 2π.
(a) Find cos θ.
(b) Hence find the exact value of −2 sin θ cos θ − 1 cos 2θ.
items.markingKey: (a) cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ (M1), negative/positive by quadrant 4 (R1), 24/25 (A1). (b) sin θ cos θ = −168/625, cos 2θ = 527/625 (A1 A1); −191/625 (A1).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "cosecant (cosec x)"?
options: The angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc equal in length to the radius; π radians = 180°
The identity cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 for all θ, from x² + y² = 1 on the unit circle
The ratio sin θ / cos θ, i.e. the gradient of the radius to the point (cos θ, sin θ); undefined when cos θ = 0
The reciprocal of sine: cosec x = 1/sin x, defined where sin x ≠ 0
items.answer: The reciprocal of sine: cosec x = 1/sin x, defined where sin x ≠ 0
items.markingKey: D. "cosecant (cosec x)" is the reciprocal of sine: cosec x = 1/sin x, defined where sin x ≠ 0.

items.stem: Explain why sec x can never take a value between −1 and 1.
items.answer: |cos x| ≤ 1, so |sec x| = 1/|cos x| ≥ 1; values strictly between −1 and 1 are impossible.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: |cos x| ≤ 1, so |sec x| = 1/|cos x| ≥ 1; values strictly between −1 and 1 are impossible. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Kenji writes arctan(tan(5π/4)) = 5π/4. Explain why this is incorrect and find the correct exact value.
items.markingKey: tan(5π/4) = 1 (A1); the range of arctan is (−π/2, π/2) and 5π/4 is outside it (R1); arctan(1) = π/4 (A1).

items.stem: Find the exact value of sec(arcsin(2/3)).
items.markingKey: Let θ = arcsin(2/3), so θ ∈ [−π/2, π/2] (R1); right-angled triangle or Pythagorean identity for the other ratio (M1); sign from the range of arcsin (R1); 3√5/5 (A1).

items.stem: Given that tan θ = 3/4 and π < θ < 3π/2, find the exact value of cosec θ.
items.markingKey: cosec²θ = 1 + cot²θ = 25/9 (M1 A1); sign chosen for quadrant 3 (R1); cosec θ = −5/3 (A1).

items.stem:
(a) Show that arctan(1/5) + arctan(2/3) = π/4.
(b) Find the exact value of tan(arctan(1/5) + arctan(2)).
(c) Hence state whether arctan(1/5) + arctan(2) is less than or greater than π/2, giving a reason.
items.answer: (a) tan of the sum = 1 and the sum lies in (0, π/2) (b) 11/3 (c) less than π/2
items.markingKey: (a) Let A = arctan(1/5), B = arctan(2/3) M1; tan(A + B) = (13/15)/(13/15) = 1 A1; A, B ∈ (0, π/4] so A + B ∈ (0, π/2) R1 AG. (b) (1/5 + 2)/(1 − 2/5) M1 = 11/3 A1. (c) both angles in (0, π/2), so the sum is in (0, π); tan of it is positive R1, so the sum is less than π/2 A1.

items.stem: Find the exact value of arctan(√3).
items.markingKey: D. arctan returns its principal value; arctan(√3) = π/3, which lies in the range of arctan.

items.stem: A student claims: "cot x = tan(1/x)." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: cot x = 1/tan x = cos x/sin x; it is the reciprocal of tan x, not tan of a reciprocal.
items.markingKey: cot x = 1/tan x = cos x/sin x; it is the reciprocal of tan x, not tan of a reciprocal. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Ana writes arccos(cos(7π/6)) = 7π/6. Explain why this is incorrect and find the correct exact value.
items.markingKey: cos(7π/6) = −√3/2 (A1); the range of arccos is [0, π] and 7π/6 is outside it (R1); arccos(−√3/2) = 5π/6 (A1).

items.stem: A student claims: "arcsin(1/2) = 5π/6, because sin(5π/6) = 1/2." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: arcsin has range [−π/2, π/2], so arcsin(1/2) = π/6; 5π/6 is another solution of sin x = 1/2 but not the principal value.
items.markingKey: arcsin has range [−π/2, π/2], so arcsin(1/2) = π/6; 5π/6 is another solution of sin x = 1/2 but not the principal value. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Given that tan θ = −8/15 and π/2 < θ < π, find the exact value of cosec θ.
items.markingKey: cosec²θ = 1 + cot²θ = 289/64 (M1 A1); sign chosen for quadrant 2 (R1); cosec θ = 17/8 (A1).

items.stem: Find the exact value of tan(arccos(−5/13)).
items.markingKey: Let θ = arccos(−5/13), so θ ∈ [0, π] (R1); right-angled triangle or Pythagorean identity for the other ratio (M1); sign from the range of arccos (R1); −12/5 (A1).

items.stem:
Let α = arcsin(7/25) and β = arccos(4/5).
(a) Find the exact values of cos α and sin β.
(b) Find the exact value of sin(α + β).
(c) Find the exact value of cos(α + β).
(d) Hence determine whether α + β is greater or less than π/2, justifying your answer.
items.answer: (a) cos α = 24/25, sin β = 3/5 (b) 4/5 (c) 3/5 (d) less than π/2
items.markingKey: (a) α, β acute (R1); cos α = 24/25 A1, sin β = 3/5 A1. (b) compound angle formula M1, 4/5 A1. (c) 3/5 A1. (d) α + β ∈ (0, π) and cos(α + β) > 0 R1 so α + β is less than π/2 A1.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "compound angle identity for cosine".
items.answer: The identity cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B (note the sign change)
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the identity cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B (note the sign change). Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Explain how the identity for sin 2θ follows from the compound angle identity.
items.answer: Put B = A in sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B to get sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Put B = A in sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B to get sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Omar says that sin(π/6 + π/2) = sin(π/6) + sin(π/2) = 3/2. Explain the error and find the correct exact value of sin(2π/3).
items.markingKey: sin is not linear, so it does not distribute over addition (R1); correct compound angle identity (M1); exact substitution (A1); sin(2π/3) = √3/2 (A1).

items.stem: Angles A and B are such that sin A = 8/17 with 0 < A < π/2, and cos B = 12/13 with 3π/2 < B < 2π. Find the exact value of cos(A − B).
items.markingKey: cos A = 15/17 (A1), sin B = −5/13 (A1) with correct signs; correct expansion of cos(A − B) (M1); 140/221 (A1).

items.stem: A student claims: "cos(A + B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: The sign is reversed: cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B.
items.markingKey: The sign is reversed: cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
(a) By writing sin 3θ as sin(2θ + θ), show that sin 3θ ≡ 3 sin θ − 4 sin³θ.
(b) Given that sin θ = 1/3, find the exact value of sin 3θ.
items.markingKey: (a) sin 2θ cos θ + cos 2θ sin θ M1; 2 sin θ cos²θ + (1 − 2sin²θ) sin θ A1; cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ M1; simplifies to 3 sin θ − 4sin³θ AG. (b) 3(1/3) − 4(1/3)³ M1 = 23/27 A1.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "compound angle identity for cosine"?
options: The identity sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B
The identity tan 2θ = 2 tan θ/(1 − tan²θ), valid when tan²θ ≠ 1
The reciprocal of sine: cosec x = 1/sin x, defined where sin x ≠ 0
The identity cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B (note the sign change)
items.answer: The identity cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B (note the sign change)
items.markingKey: D. "compound angle identity for cosine" is the identity cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B (note the sign change).

items.stem: Explain why the formula tan 2θ = 2 tan θ/(1 − tan²θ) cannot be used when θ = 7π/4, and state what happens to tan 2θ there.
items.answer: tan²(7π/4) = 1 so the denominator is 0; 2θ = 7π/2 where tan is undefined.
items.markingKey: tan(7π/4) = −1 so 1 − tan²θ = 0 (R1); 2θ = 7π/2 is an odd multiple of π/2 (A1) where tan 2θ is undefined (R1).

items.stem: Show that sin(x − π/4) can be written as (√2/2) sin x − (√2/2) cos x.
items.markingKey: Correct compound angle identity (M1); exact values cos(π/4) = √2/2, sin(π/4) = √2/2 substituted (A1); result (√2/2) sin x − (√2/2) cos x AG (A1).

items.stem: Omar says that sin(π/6 + π/4) = sin(π/6) + sin(π/4) = (1 + √2)/2. Explain the error and find the correct exact value of sin(5π/12).
items.markingKey: sin is not linear, so it does not distribute over addition (R1); correct compound angle identity (M1); exact substitution (A1); sin(5π/12) = (√2 + √6)/4 (A1).

items.stem: Given that tan θ = −1/3, find the exact value of tan 2θ.
items.markingKey: Correct identity for tan 2θ (M1); substitution of −1/3 (A1); −3/4 (A1).

items.stem: By writing 11π/12 as π/4 + 2π/3, find the exact value of sin 11π/12.
items.markingKey: Correct compound angle identity for sin (M1); exact values of sin/cos of the two angles substituted (A1); simplified: (−√2 + √6)/4 (A1).

items.stem:
The acute angles A and B satisfy tan A = 1/7 and tan B = 3/4.
(a) Show that tan(A + B) = 1.
(b) Hence find the exact value of A + B, justifying your answer.
(c) Find the exact value of tan 2A.
(d) Find the exact value of tan(2A + B).
items.markingKey: (a) tan(A + B) formula M1, numerator 25/28 and denominator 25/28 A1, = 1 AG. (b) A, B acute so 0 < A + B < π R1; A + B = π/4 A1. (c) tan 2A = 2tan A/(1 − tan²A) M1 = 7/24 A1. (d) 2A + B = A + π/4 so tan = (tan A + 1)/(1 − tan A) M1 = 4/3 A1.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "odd function"?
options: The reciprocal of sine: cosec x = 1/sin x, defined where sin x ≠ 0
The angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc equal in length to the radius; π radians = 180°
The reciprocal of cosine: sec x = 1/cos x, defined where cos x ≠ 0
A function with f(−x) = −f(x) for all x in its domain; its graph has rotational symmetry of order 2 about the origin (e.g. sin x, tan x)
items.answer: A function with f(−x) = −f(x) for all x in its domain; its graph has rotational symmetry of order 2 about the origin (e.g. sin x, tan x)
items.markingKey: D. "odd function" is a function with f(−x) = −f(x) for all x in its domain; its graph has rotational symmetry of order 2 about the origin (e.g. sin x, tan x).

items.stem: Kenji writes: "x sin x is odd because sin x is odd." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: x is odd and sin x is odd; (−x)sin(−x) = x sin x, so the product is even.
items.markingKey: x is odd and sin x is odd; (−x)sin(−x) = x sin x, so the product is even. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Use the symmetry of the unit circle to find the value of Σ (k = 0 to 9) sin(2πk/10).
items.markingKey: The angles 2πk/10 are equally spaced, so the points pair up symmetrically (opposite points for even 10) (R1); contributions cancel (M1); sum = 0 (A1).

items.stem: Given that cos α = 0.54, write down the value of (a) cos(−α), (b) sin(α + π/2), (c) cos(π + α).
items.markingKey: A1 for each correct value, using the symmetries of the unit circle / graph: cos(−α) = 0.54; sin(α + π/2) = 0.54; cos(π + α) = −0.54.

items.stem: For each function, determine whether it is odd, even or neither, justifying your answer algebraically: (a) f(x) = x² tan x (b) g(x) = e^x sin x.
items.markingKey: For each: substitute −x (M1), use sin(−x) = −sin x, cos(−x) = cos x, tan(−x) = −tan x (A1), compare with f(x) and −f(x) and conclude (R1). (a) odd (b) neither. For "neither", a numerical counter-example (e.g. x = π/4) is required.

items.stem: Define the term "even function".
items.answer: A function with f(−x) = f(x) for all x in its domain; its graph is symmetric in the y-axis (e.g. cos x)

items.stem: Explain why the product of an odd function and an even function is odd.
items.answer: If f is odd and g is even, (fg)(−x) = f(−x)g(−x) = −f(x)g(x) = −(fg)(x).
items.markingKey: Award marks for: If f is odd and g is even, (fg)(−x) = f(−x)g(−x) = −f(x)g(x) = −(fg)(x). (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Tomás writes: "cos(π − θ) = cos θ." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Reflecting in the y-axis changes the sign of the x-coordinate: cos(π − θ) = −cos θ.
items.markingKey: Reflecting in the y-axis changes the sign of the x-coordinate: cos(π − θ) = −cos θ. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why the formula tan 2θ = 2 tan θ/(1 − tan²θ) cannot be used when θ = 3π/4, and state what happens to tan 2θ there.

items.stem: Without evaluating either side, explain why sin(2π − π/6) = −sin(π/6).

items.stem: Using the unit circle, explain why cos(4π/3) is negative and hence write down its exact value.
items.markingKey: 4π/3 lies in quadrant 3 (R1); the reference angle is π/3 (A1); in quadrant 3 the x-value makes cos negative (R1); so cos(4π/3) = −1/2 (A1).

items.stem: Show that (1 − cos 2x)/sin 2x ≡ tan x.
items.answer: (1 − cos 2x)/sin 2x = 2sin²x/(2 sin x cos x) = tan x
items.markingKey: 1 − cos 2x = 2sin²x (M1 A1); sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x (A1); cancel to sin x/cos x = tan x AG.

items.stem: "sec x is the inverse function of cos x." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: sec x = 1/cos x is the reciprocal; the inverse function is arccos x.

items.stem: Explain how tan(A + B) is derived from the sine and cosine compound angle identities.
items.answer: tan(A + B) = sin(A + B)/cos(A + B); divide numerator and denominator by cos A cos B to obtain (tan A + tan B)/(1 − tan A tan B).
